steps.domain_action: Initialize the system with separate peptide and glycan precursors in the reaction space.
Split the domain into two distinct words: the peptide bulk and the glycan boundary.
Advance the peptide arm via nucleophilic attack from the amine or hydroxyl group.
Affirm the high kinetic barrier that prevents spontaneous rearrangement of the forming bond.
Descend the glycan arm via acceptance at the anomeric carbon, establishing the chiral center.
Refute non-matching chiral configurations, enforcing persistent orientational memory.
Compose the two arms into a single glycosidic linkage, joining the peptide and glycan words.
Establish the self-referential identity of the anomeric carbon interface where chemical identities merge.
Hold the asymmetric topology where the single boundary structure connects to the bulk, maintaining both states simultaneously.
Fix the non-trivial integer winding number of the topological link, making it irreversible without bond breakage.
Fuse the peptide and glycan arms into a single receptor binding surface, creating a functional unit with scale-free sensitivity.
Anchor the final glycopeptide complex as a closed boundary containing the whole system.

phase_6.cycle_cost: The activation energy required to overcome the kinetic barrier and form the covalent bond.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Two separate, high-entropy molecules (peptide and glycan) with independent conformational spaces.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A single, lower-entropy glycopeptide complex with constrained conformational freedom due to the rigid chiral bond.
